summary: Add written redox practice and a concise explanation of the nitrate bookkeeping that examiners identify as difficult.

improvements.why: The core set has many coefficient MCQs but no structured item requiring the learner to show oxidation-number changes, balance the whole equation, and check charge or atom counts; ER 9701 s21 P13 Q9 highlights the extra nitrate ions needed in copper and nitric acid.
improvements.what: Add one structured, mark-scheme-style balance of Cu with dilute nitric acid to form Cu(NO3)2, NO and H2O, asking for the Cu and N oxidation-number changes, electron ratio, full coefficients and final atom check; add one distinct ionic equation in acidic or alkaline conditions requiring an explicit charge check. Provide three non-answer-revealing hints and explanations for both.

improvements.where: note, after the Worked example in ## Method
improvements.why: The current method explains electron matching but does not show that a reactant may have a second role in the final molecular equation; ER 9701 s21 P13 Q9 reports that candidates counted only the nitric acid reduced to NO.
improvements.source: ER 9701 s21 P13 Q9 in bundle
improvements.what: Add a short worked comparison for 3Cu + 8HNO3 -> 3Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO + 4H2O: three Cu atoms release six electrons; two nitrate N atoms gain six, while six more nitrate ions supply the three Cu(NO3)2 units. Show why the acid coefficient is eight.

improvements.why: Roman numeral notation has seven retrieval variants but the core practice is mostly recognition, with no learner-produced chemical name justified from a formula.
improvements.what: Add a short-answer item requiring a compound name with a Roman numeral and a one-line oxidation-number calculation for a fresh formula; mark the numeral as the magnitude per atom, not the number of atoms.
